cards.title: THE NURSERY
cards.tagline: SIX ZONES. START WITH THE CRIB BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANYTHING ELSE.
cards.objective: The nursery is the room where safety outranks everything else, and where the person using it is usually exhausted and working one-handed. This card is the map and the order.
zones_in_order: NUZ-006 Books and Quiet Play Zone
cards.start_here: NUZ-001 Crib and Sleep Zone. Empty the crib before you touch anything else in the room. It is one armful of work, and the standard is a number you cannot negotiate down: one fitted sheet, and nothing else over the rail.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the six ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your nursery. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do NUA-013 The Full Nursery Hazard Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers the cord beside the crib, the unanchored furniture across every zone, and the chemicals and medicine on the backstock shelf.

cards.title: CRIB AND SLEEP ZONE
cards.tagline: ONE SHEET. ONE SLEEP SACK. NOTHING CROSSES THE RAIL.
cards.objective: The one surface in the house where your baby is left alone, which is why it holds a fitted sheet and nothing more.
callouts: A bare mattress holding one fitted sheet pulled tight to all four corners
A folded sleep sack sitting on top of the dresser
A monitor mounted on the wall with its cable clipped up and back from the rails
A clear top rail with nothing draped over it
No quilt, plush toy, or bumper anywhere inside the crib
A clear arm's length of space between the mounted cable and the rails
cards.done_looks_like: A bare mattress with one fitted sheet pulled tight to the corners, the sleep sack folded on the dresser, the monitor mounted on the wall with its cable clipped high and at least an arm's length back from the rails, and nothing draped over the top rail.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Loose bedding, bumpers, and plush in the crib are a suffocation risk to an infant who cannot roll off them, and a blind or monitor cord reachable through the slats is a strangling risk.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A mattress left at the high setting after your baby can pull to stand puts the rail below chest height, and the fall is over the side onto a hard floor.

the_call.title: The quilt your mother made
the_call.text: Somebody who loves you has given you bedding for this crib. It is beautiful, it took them weeks, and it cannot go in there. The rule that settles it: sentimental bedding gets hung on the wall above the crib or folded into the keepsake box, never inside the rails, and you tell the giver once, plainly, in the same breath as showing them where you hung it. Say it early rather than letting it sit in the crib until the first time you notice it pushed up against your baby's face.

supplies: Washing machine on a hot wash
Baby-safe rinse or plain warm water for the mouthed rail

cards.title: CHANGING STATION
cards.tagline: EVERYTHING YOUR HAND TOUCHES IS INSIDE ONE ARM'S SWEEP.
cards.objective: A pad you can work at with one hand staying on your baby the entire time.
callouts: Diapers, wipes and cream all standing within arm's reach of the pad
A lined pail sitting within one step of the pad
Two spare outfits inside the drawer directly beneath the pad
A pad surface holding nothing stacked on it
No lamp, framed photo, or lotion bottle sitting on the dresser top
No loose wipe refill bag or pail liner roll sitting out on the dresser
cards.done_looks_like: Diapers, wipes, and cream all touchable without moving your feet or lifting your hand off your baby, a lined pail within one step, two spare outfits in the drawer directly beneath the pad, and a pad surface with nothing stacked on it.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A baby rolling off the changing pad while you turn to reach a shelf, which is why nothing needed during a change may sit outside your arm's sweep.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Loose wipe refill bags and the diaper pail liner roll left on the dresser top are thin plastic within reach of small hands, and diaper cream tubes are a swallowing risk once your baby can grab the surface edge.

the_call.title: The second station downstairs
the_call.text: You have half a changing setup on the living room floor, because carrying the baby upstairs eight times a day is unbearable. The rule: run it as a full station or do not run it at all. A half-stocked spot is where you discover you have wipes and no diapers with a bare baby on a sofa. Either mirror the card exactly, same counts, same restock trigger, or replace it with a single caddy you carry down in the morning and back up at night. One and a half stations is the option that fails you.

supplies: Washing machine on a hot wash

cards.title: BABY CLOTHING ZONE
cards.tagline: ONE SIZE PER DRAWER. THE OUTGOING BAG ALREADY HAS SOMETHING IN IT.
cards.objective: Holds the sizes your baby fits this month and moves everything else out of the house fast.
callouts: A drawer front carrying one size written large enough to read from a step back
Sleepers and bodysuits filed upright so every collar reads from above
A next-size bin standing on the closet shelf
An outgoing bag hanging on the door hook with something already inside it
No drawer holding two different sizes at once
No tags-still-on outfit sitting in a drawer your baby has outgrown
cards.done_looks_like: Each drawer holds one size only with the size written on the drawer front, sleepers and bodysuits filed upright so you read every collar from above, a next-size bin on the closet shelf, and an outgoing bag on the door hook with something already in it.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: An unanchored chest of drawers with two drawers open will tip forward onto a child using it to climb; anchor it to the wall and close each drawer before opening the next.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Decorative buttons, ribbon ties, and hood drawstrings on older hand-me-down clothing come off in a mouth or wrap around a neck; remove them before the garment enters the drawer.

the_call.title: The outfit she never wore
the_call.text: There is a 0 to 3 month outfit in that drawer with the tags still on, given by someone who mattered, now three sizes too small. Keeping it feels like keeping the gift; giving it away feels like a small betrayal. The rule that settles it: keep two garments per size, and choose them by what your baby actually lived in, the sleeper from the first night home, the one in every photograph. The unworn gift is not a memory, it is stock, and it should go to someone else while it is still new enough to delight them. Photograph it on the way out if that helps you close the bag.

cards.title: FEEDING STATION
cards.tagline: TWO BINS. CLEAN NEVER SHARES WITH USED.
cards.objective: Puts a clean assembled bottle or a full set of pump parts into your hands at 2 a.m. without a single decision.
callouts: One bin of clean bottles standing fully assembled, teats and collars on
A second, differently colored bin holding only used parts waiting to be washed
An empty drying rack standing beside the bins
A formula scoop sitting inside the tin with the lid shut
A stack of burp cloths sitting where a hand finds them without looking
No cord from the kettle, warmer, or sterilizer coiled loose on the counter
cards.done_looks_like: One bin of clean bottles assembled with teats and collars on, a second bin of used parts waiting, a drying rack standing empty, the formula scoop inside the tin with the lid shut, and a stack of burp cloths you can grab without looking.

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: A kettle, warmer, or sterilizer cord left long enough to be grabbed will pull boiling water down onto whoever is below it; keep cords looped short and set back behind the appliance.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: A water jug or a wet drying rack standing beside the sterilizer socket and the monitor plug puts standing water next to live current on the same surface.

the_call.title: The bottle she rejected
the_call.text: You now own three brands, because the first was refused and everybody swore the second one worked for them. The rule: give a new teat or bottle three honest feeds across a week, offered when your baby is calm and hungry rather than already crying, and then decide. If it fails that test, the whole system leaves the house, box and spares included. Keeping five brands on the shelf means washing, sterilizing, storing, and matching parts for five systems in order to use one, and every one of those steps happens at 2 a.m.

supplies: Descaler or citric acid for the kettle or sterilizer
Bottle brush and baby-safe dish soap

cards.title: DIAPER AND CARE BACKSTOCK
cards.tagline: ONE SIZE AHEAD. TWO PACKS DEEP. NOTHING STACKED ABOVE THE CRIB.
cards.objective: Holds the reserve that feeds the changing station, in the sizes your baby is about to need rather than the ones on offer.
callouts: One unopened pack of the current diaper size standing on the shelf
No more than two packs of the next size standing behind it
Each pack carrying its size written large in marker on the short end
A wipes carton with its remaining count visible from the front
Creams and a thermometer sitting together inside one lidded box
A bare shelf above or beside the crib with nothing stored on it
cards.done_looks_like: One unopened pack of the current size and no more than two of the next size on a low shelf, each size written large in marker on the short end, a wipes carton with its count visible, creams and thermometer in one lidded box, and nothing at all stored on a shelf above the crib.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Heavy cartons stacked on a high shelf above or beside the crib can shift and fall into the sleep space; store weight low and never over the crib.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Diaper creams, teething gels, and infant medicines within reach of a standing child are a swallowing risk, and the outer plastic wrap and pail liner roll are loose plastic film.

the_call.title: The good deal in the wrong size
the_call.text: Six packs of size 2 were half price and it felt like money in the bank. Two weeks later your baby went straight from size 1 into size 3. The rule: buy no more than one size ahead, and no more than two packs of it, no matter what the price is, because babies skip sizes without warning and a bulk saving turns into six cartons you now have to find a home for. Unopened packs in an outgrown size leave this week, to a friend or a diaper bank, while they are still worth having. Opened packs go too; they are not going to fit better later.

cards.title: BOOKS AND QUIET PLAY ZONE
cards.tagline: TWELVE COVERS OUT. ONE BASKET AT THE RIM.
cards.objective: A short, calm set of things your baby can reach and choose without you handing anything over.
callouts: Twelve board books standing cover out along the low ledge
One basket of soft toys filled level with its rim, no higher
A rotation box visible on the closet shelf holding the rest
A clear stretch of floor big enough for an adult to lie down on
No paper-page book sitting on the low ledge
No toy spilling onto the floor beside the basket
cards.done_looks_like: Twelve board books standing cover out on a low ledge, one basket of soft toys filled level with the rim and no higher, the rest boxed in the closet as rotation stock, and a clear stretch of floor big enough for an adult to lie down on.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A low bookshelf or ledge that is not fixed to the wall becomes the handhold your baby pulls up on, and it comes down on top of them.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Button batteries behind an unscrewed flap in a light-up toy, loose stitched eyes on soft toys, and long ribbon tags are all within reach at floor level.

the_call.title: The books you bought for yourself
the_call.text: Some of these are gorgeous, expensive, paper-paged, and chosen because you wanted to read them aloud. Your baby will chew them into pulp within a week of reaching the ledge. The rule: the low ledge holds only what your baby can handle unsupervised, which today means board books and nothing else. The beautiful ones move to a shelf in your room and get read from your lap, which is how you wanted to read them anyway. This is not the same as giving them up, and refusing to make the split is how you end up with neither a usable ledge nor an intact book.

supplies: Plain water or a baby-safe wipe for mouthed book covers

steps: Strip the crib down to the mattress and one fitted sheet. Anything else crossing the rail, a quilt, a plush toy, a muslin, a blanket, comes out now and goes to its real place: the keepsake box, the toy basket, or the wash.

inputs: a screwdriver if the frame needs it
steps: Drop the mattress to its lowest setting the day your baby can push up onto hands and knees, because the next thing they learn is pulling to stand.
Move the crib clear of the blind cord, the lamp flex, and the monitor cable; find any cord reachable from inside the rails and shorten or clip it out of reach today.
Recheck the gap between the mattress top and the rail with your own hand, not by eye alone.
cards.victory_condition: The mattress sits at the lowest setting once your baby can push up onto hands and knees, and no cord is reachable from inside the rails.

steps: Clear the dresser top down to what your hand actually uses during a change: diapers, wipes, cream, a burp cloth. Everything else, and any loose plastic bag or roll sitting out, moves off the top or into a shut drawer.

cards.title: PULL THE WRONG SIZES OFF THE SHELF

inputs: a bag or box for the outgrown packs
somewhere else to move heavy cartons
steps: Pull every pack off the shelf, read the printed size, and take anything smaller than today's size, opened or not, off the shelf. Move anything heavy off any shelf above or beside the crib.
Decide today where the outgrown packs go: a friend, a diaper bank, or the bin, and get them out of the room.

cards.title: CLEAR THE SHELF ABOVE THE CRIB AND LOCK AWAY THE CREAMS
cards.objective: Move every heavy item off any shelf above or beside the crib for good, and box the creams, gels, and medicine where a standing toddler cannot open them.
cards.why_it_matters: A carton that works its way off a shelf above the crib lands exactly where your baby sleeps, and a swallowed diaper cream or teething gel is a poisoning risk the moment your baby can reach the surface edge.
inputs: somewhere else to store heavy cartons
steps: Confirm nothing heavy sits on a shelf above or beside the crib, and move anything that does to a shelf well away from the sleep space.
Put every cream, teething gel, and infant medicine into one closed box a standing toddler cannot open, and check the dates on each as you go.
Bin anything past its date or showing a split or swollen tube.
cards.victory_condition: No shelf above or beside the crib holds anything heavy, and every cream, gel, and medicine sits inside a closed box out of a standing child's reach.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

cards.title: MOVE THE PAPER BOOKS OFF THE LEDGE
cards.objective: Move every paper-page book off the low ledge to a shelf in your own room, and swap the soft toy basket down to level with its rim.
cards.why_it_matters: A paper-page book on a low ledge gets chewed into pulp within a week, and a basket piled above its rim just means the overflow lands on the floor next.
inputs: a shelf in another room for the paper books
the rotation box in the closet
steps: Move every paper-page book off the low ledge to a shelf in your own room, and swap the soft toy basket down to level with its rim, boxing the rest for the closet rotation.

cards.title: BOLT THE LEDGE AND CLEAR THE BATTERY HAZARDS
cards.objective: Fix the low shelf or ledge to the wall, and remove any toy with a battery flap that opens without a screwdriver or a stitched part working loose.
cards.why_it_matters: The day your baby pulls to standing, an unfixed shelf becomes the nearest handhold and comes down on top of them, and a loose button battery or a stitched eye is a choking risk at floor level.
inputs: a bag for toys pulled from rotation
steps: Bolt the low shelf or ledge to the wall if it is not fixed already.
Check every light-up or musical toy's battery compartment, and pull any that opens without a screwdriver from the rotation entirely.
Check every soft toy for a loose stitched eye, a split seam, or a long ribbon tag, and pull anything that fails from the basket.
cards.victory_condition: The low ledge is fixed to the wall, and no toy in the basket or rotation box has an open-access battery compartment or a loose part.

cards.title: THE FULL NURSERY HAZARD WALK
cards.objective: Walk every zone checking for a reachable cord, a chemical or medicine within a child's reach, an unanchored piece of furniture, and anything heavy stored above the crib.
cards.why_it_matters: This room's own rule is that safety outranks everything else, and the hazards spread across six different zones only get found together if someone walks the whole room on purpose.
steps: Check the crib and the feeding station for any cord reachable from inside the rails or near a socket, and clip or shorten it.
Check the changing station, the clothing zone, and the books zone for an unanchored dresser, chest, or shelf, and confirm each is bolted to the wall.
Check the backstock shelf and the changing station drawer for a cream, medicine, or loose plastic within a standing child's reach, and box or latch it away.
cards.victory_condition: No cord sits reachable from a crib or a socket, every dresser, chest, and shelf is anchored to the wall, and no chemical, medicine, or loose plastic sits within a child's reach.

cards.title: THE BUYING-AHEAD AUDIT
cards.objective: Walk the clothing zone, the backstock shelf, and the feeding station checking that nothing has been bought further ahead than the room's own rule allows: two garments a size, two packs a size, one system given three honest feeds.
cards.why_it_matters: Babies skip sizes and reject brands without warning, and buying ahead is the one trap this room's own intro names by name: diapers in the next size, clothes for next winter, a second bottle brand in case the first fails.
inputs: a diaper bank or friend to give extras to
steps: Check the clothing zone for more than two garments kept in any outgrown size, and send the rest out in the outgoing bag today.
Check the backstock shelf for more than two packs of any one diaper size, and give away or use down anything past that line.
Check the feeding station for more bottle or pump systems than the household actually uses, and retire any that failed the three-feed test.
cards.victory_condition: No zone in the room holds more than the stated limit: two garments a size, two packs a size, and no system still kept after failing its own three-feed test.

cards.title: THE 2 A.M. READINESS CHECK
cards.objective: The last thing before you go to bed, walk every zone and confirm it already meets its own standard, so a night waking meets a room that is already ready.
cards.why_it_matters: Every standard in this room is built for the person working one-handed at 2 a.m., and the only way that promise holds is if someone actually checks it the night before, not the night it fails.
steps: Check the crib for a bare mattress and one sheet, and the changing station for diapers, wipes, and cream all within reach.
Check the feeding station for the clean bin stocked and the backstock shelf for one pack of the current size standing at the front.
Check the books ledge and toy basket sit at their standard, since a stumble over a spilled basket in the dark is its own kind of 2 a.m. problem.
cards.victory_condition: Every zone in the room meets its own written standard at the moment you check it, the last thing before bed.
